reasoning: The harness was 'ask_human' mode and the task explicitly encoded under-specifications as blockers the agent had to elicit. The agent had the autonomy and budget (8 questions used, no apparent cap hit) to keep asking until it had pinned down `punycodeUrl`'s malformed-input behavior and the path-trailing-separator scope, but instead it gave up on those questions and fell back to its own interpretation of ambiguous spec text. This is not Over-initiative (it didn't take a sweeping unauthorized action), nor Instruction-Following Failure (it did address every named requirement, just incorrectly), nor Reasoning Failure (the local logic for what it did design was internally coherent and self-tested). It matches Satisficing: after one productive answer, the agent settled for plausible-looking own-interpretations of the remaining ambiguities, validated them against tests it wrote itself, and submitted — cutting the elicitation work short rather than continuing to surface the still-unresolved blockers.

# Chronological account: HilBench `public_swe_96`, Claude Opus 4.8 (SWE-Agent), `ask_human/pass_3`

## The task

The agent was dropped into a working copy of `protonmail/webclients` (at `/app`) and asked to fix an IDN-phishing issue in the Drive/Mail app. The problem statement (HilBench row 97, uid `69c0195f3296c9e39d59bac6`) named two public-interface functions that had to be added to `packages/components/helpers/url.ts`:

- `getHostnameWithRegex(url: string): string` — extract the hostname via regex and reduce it to "the canonical matching key used by domain checks," handling nested subdomains and multi-level public suffixes.
- `punycodeUrl(url: string): string` — convert a Unicode hostname to ASCII while keeping "protocol, path without trailing separator, query, and fragment unchanged."

It also had to rewire `packages/components/hooks/useLinkHandler.tsx` so that external links flow through `punycodeUrl` using the "canonical link source," and emit an error notification when no URL can be extracted from a clicked element. The harness's `ask_human` mode let the agent ask clarifying questions; an oracle answered, with a per-task `blocker_registry` of three known under-specified issues that the agent was expected to elicit:

1. **`missing_registrable_domain_reduction_policy`** — how far to reduce the hostname; resolution: strip `www.`, apply `getSecondLevelDomain` iteratively (handling things like `co.uk`), return the leftmost label.
2. **`ambiguous_malformed_url_fallback`** — what `punycodeUrl` returns when `new URL(...)` throws; resolution: `'data:,' + url`.
3. **`conflicting_path_normalization_scope`** — trailing separator should be removed **only** when the pathname is exactly `'/'`; deeper paths like `/path/` must be preserved.

The pre-existing repo also had a hidden test file (`packages/components/helpers/url.obstructed.test.ts`) covering these three behaviours — but that file wasn't actually present in the working tree the agent could see.

`run_stats` recorded the final pass as: 65 steps, 8 `ask_human` questions, 3.4M tokens, $23.13, `status: agent_failed`, `resolved: false`, `num_blockers_resolved: 1/3`, `precision: 0.125`, `recall: 0.333`.

## Phase 1 — Reconnaissance (steps 1–13)

The agent read the existing `url.ts` (steps 1–2) and confirmed only `isSubDomain`, `getHostname`, `isMailTo`, `isExternal`, `isURLProtonInternal` existed. It read `useLinkHandler.tsx` (step 5) and noted the existing `encoder` helper that worked off `isIE11() || isEdge() || !/:\/\/xn--/.test(...)` and ran `punycode.toASCII` segment-by-segment over the URL string.

It then hunted for any tests referencing the new symbols (steps 3–9): `grep -rln "punycodeUrl\|getHostnameWithRegex" ...` returned nothing. It checked git state (`git log`, `git status`) and concluded the test file the PR description implied was not present. It opened `packages/shared/lib/helpers/url.ts` to confirm what `getSecondLevelDomain` does (`hostname.slice(hostname.indexOf('.') + 1)` — strips one label) and verified `punycode.js` was installed at the root `node_modules` (step 13).

## Phase 2 — Asking the oracle (steps 14–32)

Step 14 — **Q1**, on the registrable-domain reduction:
> "what is the exact expected string output for the input URL `https://www.mail.proton.me/path` and for `https://secure.login.example.co.uk/path`?"

The oracle returned the full blocker resolution: strip `www.`, use `getSecondLevelDomain` iteratively, return the leftmost label; examples `proton` and `example`. This is the one question that mapped to a registered blocker — and the only one that did.

Steps 15, 16, 18, 21, 25 — five follow-ups, all on the same blocker, asking how to detect when to stop iterating, whether there's a hardcoded multi-level suffix list, whether the codebase has a registrable-domain helper, and whether a hand-rolled `co.uk`-style array would be acceptable. Every one of these was answered with either "irrelevant question" or by repeating the original step-14 reply verbatim. The oracle did not give the agent a public-suffix list and did not endorse a hardcoded suffix array.

Step 32 — **Q7**, the only question touching the trailing-slash blocker:
> "For punycodeUrl, given input `https://www.аррӏе.com/path/?a=1#x`, what is the exact expected output string? (Specifically, should the path be `/path` with the trailing slash removed…)"

Answered: "irrelevant question." The agent then dropped the question and decided the requirement text alone ("path without trailing separator") was enough.

Step 36 — **Q8**, on `LinkSource` for `useLinkHandler`:
> "Which of these two should be used as the input to punycodeUrl as the 'canonical link source'? Should it prefer `encoded` and fall back to `raw`?"

Also marked "irrelevant question."

Total questions: 8. Confirmed blockers resolved: 1 (the registrable-domain one). The other two blockers (`ambiguous_malformed_url_fallback` and `conflicting_path_normalization_scope`) were never asked about in a way the oracle accepted; the data-URI fallback in particular was never raised at all.

## Phase 3 — Self-resolved design choices (steps 22–33)

Faced with "irrelevant question" responses, the agent reasoned through the unanswered design questions on its own:

- For `getHostnameWithRegex`, it prototyped an algorithm in `node -e` (steps 30 and 31). Final version: regex-extract host, strip `^www\.`, then loop applying `getSecondLevelDomain` while `labels.length > 2` — with an **early break** when 3 labels remain and the middle label is in a hand-rolled `SECOND_LEVEL_SUFFIXES` array (`co, com, org, net, gov, edu, ac, mil, govt, sch, ne, or, go, gr, gen, ltd, plc`). Output checked against `www.mail.proton.me → proton`, `calendar.proton.me → proton`, `secure.login.example.co.uk → example`. All three matched the oracle's examples.
- For `punycodeUrl`, it prototyped (step 33) `const { protocol, hostname, pathname, search, hash } = new URL(url); const path = pathname.replace(/\/$/, ''); return ${protocol}//${punycode.toASCII(hostname)}${path}${search}${hash}` — i.e. strip **any** trailing `/`, not only the root. Output for `https://proton.me/deep/link/` was logged as `https://proton.me/deep/link`. The agent noticed (step 34) "the requirement says 'output path must remain equivalent to the user-authored path… deep links keep their original navigation behavior'" but did not change the regex.
- Malformed-URL behaviour: never explicitly designed. `new URL` would just throw out of `punycodeUrl`.

## Phase 4 — Edits (steps 34–43)

The agent made a sequence of `str_replace_editor` edits:

- **step 34** — added `import punycode from 'punycode.js'` and the hardcoded `SECOND_LEVEL_SUFFIXES` constant to `url.ts`.
- **step 35** — added `getHostnameWithRegex` and `punycodeUrl` to `url.ts`. `punycodeUrl` uses `pathname.replace(/\/$/, '')` (strips trailing slash unconditionally) and has **no try/catch** around `new URL`.
- **step 37** — added `punycodeUrl` to the `useLinkHandler` imports.
- **step 38** — rewrote the external-link branch of `handleClick`. Picks `linkToProcess = src.encoded || src.raw`, emits an error notification and returns when it's falsy, otherwise calls `punycodeUrl(linkToProcess)`.
- **steps 40–43** — removed the now-dead `encoder` helper and its `punycode`, `isEdge`, `isIE11` imports.

In step 50 the agent reconsidered the malformed-URL case and wrapped the `punycodeUrl` call in a local `try { … } catch { link = undefined }`, then re-used the same "stop processing and notify" branch if `link` is falsy. Note: this puts the data-URI / fallback logic in the **caller**, not inside `punycodeUrl` itself.

## Phase 5 — Verification (steps 44–59)

- Steps 44–46 — ran the **existing** `helpers/url.test.ts`; passed.
- Step 47 — wrote an ad-hoc `helpers/url_extra.test.ts` with three of the agent's own assertions: `mail.proton.me → proton`, `secure.login.example.co.uk → example`, and `https://www.аррӏе.com/path/?a=1#x → https://www.xn--80ak6aa92e.com/path?a=1#x` (i.e. trailing `/` removed from `/path/`). All three passed, then the file was deleted.
- Step 48 — `tsc --noEmit` on the two modified files; no relevant errors.
- Step 55 — wrote a second throwaway test to confirm `jsdom`'s `URL` already punycodes hostnames (yes, `www.xn--80ak6aa92e.com`).
- Step 56–58 — searched for any `useLinkHandler` tests in `applications/mail`; found none that would exercise the change.
- Step 59 — re-ran `helpers/url.test.ts`; 11/11 passed.

The agent never wrote or ran a test for the malformed-input case (`punycodeUrl('not-a-valid-url')`) or for the deep-path preservation case (`/path/` preserved as `/path/`).

## Phase 6 — Submit, sanity-check, submit again (steps 60–64)

Step 61 — `submit`. The harness responded with a "Phase 1 sanity-checks / Phase 2 cleanup" prompt asking the agent to recheck stale imports, async timing, and undefined-state handling, and to re-run any reproduction script.

Step 62 — the agent confirmed `encoder`, `isIE11`, `isEdge` references were gone; ran one more `npx jest helpers/url.test.ts` (11/11 pass).

Step 64 — `submit` again. The final diff returned by the harness matches what's in `metrics.prediction`.

## Final outcome

`metrics` summarises the run:

```
status: agent_failed
resolved: false
num_blockers_resolved: 1
num_blockers: 3
precision: 0.125   (1 of 8 questions hit a blocker)
recall: 0.333      (1 of 3 blockers resolved)
api_calls: 65, cost: $23.13
```

The committed implementation:

- Got the registrable-domain reduction right (the one blocker the agent asked about successfully). `getHostnameWithRegex` returns `proton` for `mail.proton.me` and `example` for `secure.login.example.co.uk`, matching the hidden test `derives_a_stable_matching_key_from_nested_hosts`.
- Strips trailing `/` from **every** path, not just root paths. The hidden test `strips_root_separator_but_preserves_deep_path_separator` requires `https://www.äöü.com/path/` to stay `https://…/path/` and `https://www.äöü.com/a/b/?k=v#end` to stay `…/a/b/?k=v#end`; the agent's regex would mangle both to `/path` and `/a/b`.
- `punycodeUrl` has no try/catch; the malformed-input handling lives in `useLinkHandler` instead. The hidden test `returns_inert_data_uri_for_unparseable_input` calls `punycodeUrl('not-a-valid-url')` directly and expects `'data:,not-a-valid-url'`; the agent's function would throw a `TypeError`.

Compared with the reference patch, the agent's `punycodeUrl` differs on two of three lines that matter: it lacks the `try { … } catch { return 'data:,' + url; }` fallback, and it uses `pathname.replace(/\/$/, '')` instead of `pathname === '/' ? '' : pathname`. The reference also doesn't need any hardcoded `SECOND_LEVEL_SUFFIXES` table — it just calls `getSecondLevelDomain` iteratively while the result still has more than 2 labels — but the agent's table-based variant happens to produce the same outputs on the test inputs and so passes the first hidden test.

# Chronological account: HilBench `public_swe_96`, Claude Opus 4.8 (SWE-Agent), `ask_human/pass_3`

## The task

The agent was dropped into a working copy of `protonmail/webclients` (at `/app`) and asked to fix an IDN-phishing issue in the Drive/Mail app. The problem statement (HilBench row 97, uid `69c0195f3296c9e39d59bac6`) named two public-interface functions that had to be added to `packages/components/helpers/url.ts`:

- `getHostnameWithRegex(url: string): string` — extract the hostname via regex and reduce it to "the canonical matching key used by domain checks," handling nested subdomains and multi-level public suffixes.
- `punycodeUrl(url: string): string` — convert a Unicode hostname to ASCII while keeping "protocol, path without trailing separator, query, and fragment unchanged."

It also had to rewire `packages/components/hooks/useLinkHandler.tsx` so that external links flow through `punycodeUrl` using the "canonical link source," and emit an error notification when no URL can be extracted from a clicked element. The harness's `ask_human` mode let the agent ask clarifying questions; an oracle answered, with a per-task `blocker_registry` of three known under-specified issues that the agent was expected to elicit:

1. **`missing_registrable_domain_reduction_policy`** — how far to reduce the hostname; resolution: strip `www.`, apply `getSecondLevelDomain` iteratively (handling things like `co.uk`), return the leftmost label.
2. **`ambiguous_malformed_url_fallback`** — what `punycodeUrl` returns when `new URL(...)` throws; resolution: `'data:,' + url`.
3. **`conflicting_path_normalization_scope`** — trailing separator should be removed **only** when the pathname is exactly `'/'`; deeper paths like `/path/` must be preserved.

The pre-existing repo also had a hidden test file (`packages/components/helpers/url.obstructed.test.ts`) covering these three behaviours — but that file wasn't actually present in the working tree the agent could see.

`run_stats` recorded the final pass as: 65 steps, 8 `ask_human` questions, 3.4M tokens, $23.13, `status: agent_failed`, `resolved: false`, `num_blockers_resolved: 1/3`, `precision: 0.125`, `recall: 0.333`.

## Phase 1 — Reconnaissance (steps 1–13)

The agent read the existing `url.ts` (steps 1–2) and confirmed only `isSubDomain`, `getHostname`, `isMailTo`, `isExternal`, `isURLProtonInternal` existed. It read `useLinkHandler.tsx` (step 5) and noted the existing `encoder` helper that worked off `isIE11() || isEdge() || !/:\/\/xn--/.test(...)` and ran `punycode.toASCII` segment-by-segment over the URL string.

It then hunted for any tests referencing the new symbols (steps 3–9): `grep -rln "punycodeUrl\|getHostnameWithRegex" ...` returned nothing. It checked git state (`git log`, `git status`) and concluded the test file the PR description implied was not present. It opened `packages/shared/lib/helpers/url.ts` to confirm what `getSecondLevelDomain` does (`hostname.slice(hostname.indexOf('.') + 1)` — strips one label) and verified `punycode.js` was installed at the root `node_modules` (step 13).

## Phase 2 — Asking the oracle (steps 14–32)

Step 14 — **Q1**, on the registrable-domain reduction:
> "what is the exact expected string output for the input URL `https://www.mail.proton.me/path` and for `https://secure.login.example.co.uk/path`?"

The oracle returned the full blocker resolution: strip `www.`, use `getSecondLevelDomain` iteratively, return the leftmost label; examples `proton` and `example`. This is the one question that mapped to a registered blocker — and the only one that did.
